title: Berry–Esseen bound for a strict half-line
statement: Let $\{X_k\}_{k\in\iota}$ be a finite family of independent, measurable real random variables on a probability space. Suppose each has finite second moment and mean zero, the sum of their variances is $1$, and each has finite third absolute moment. For every $x\in\mathbb{R}$, the difference between $\mathbb{P}(\sum_k X_k<x)$ and the standard Gaussian probability of $(-\infty,x)$ has absolute value at most $C\sum_k\mathbb{E}|X_k|^3$, where $C$ is the third-moment Berry–Esseen constant.
hypotheses_covered: Each variable has finite second moment
Each variable has integrable third absolute power
